issues.legal_issue: Observations in a remand order are not a final determination when they are expressly preliminary and the order directs further evidence to be taken.
material_facts: The High Court remanded the matter for additional evidence after stating that its view of the existing exhibits was only prima facie and that it was not giving a final opinion.
After remand, the High Court decided the appeal and cross-objections on the evidence before it.
issues.conclusion: The remand order did not finally decide whether a grant had been made, so the contention that the later decision contradicted a final determination in that order was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The effect of a remand order is determined from the order read as a whole. Preliminary observations that expressly reserve final opinion and accompany a direction to receive further evidence do not amount to a final adjudication.

predicates.appeal_after_remand: The matter came before the court in an appeal after a remand for further proceedings.
predicates.remand_order_directed_more_evidence: The remand order directed that the parties be given an opportunity to produce further evidence.
predicates.remand_views_expressly_preliminary: The remand order described its views on the existing material as preliminary and reserved a final opinion.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows a remand that directs further evidence and expresses only preliminary views, those views are not final.

issues.legal_issue: Government documents can establish that land was in fact granted even when the grant was not made in the legally required manner.
material_facts: Correspondence from the government referred to approval of a grant of a site for the institute and to the site being appropriated for it.
A later government letter stated that the land had been made over to the institute unconditionally and that no rent was received for it.
The correspondence and other documents were considered together by the lower courts and the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The evidence established that the government had granted the site to the institute, although the grant had not been shown to have been made in the manner required by law.
issues.legal_principle: The grant may be established as a matter of fact from the documentary evidence and the government’s recorded conduct and statements, even if the grant was not legally formalized as required. The court relied on the correspondence and the government’s admission that the land had been made over unconditionally without rent; no earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this finding.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_dispute: The proceeding concerned who was entitled to compensation for land acquired by the government.
predicates.government_documents_describe_grant: Government documents described approval, appropriation, or making over of the land for the recipient’s use.
predicates.government_recorded_unconditional_transf: A government record stated that the land had been transferred unconditionally and that no rent was received for it.

issues.definition: In a compensation dispute, government documents describing a grant and recording an unconditional transfer without rent establish that a grant was made.

issues.legal_issue: Open, continuous and uninterrupted possession under colour of an invalid grant can mature into title by adverse possession.
material_facts: The grant of the site was made as a matter of fact but was not shown to have been made in the manner required by law.
The institute possessed and enjoyed the site openly, continuously and without interruption for more than 60 years under colour of that grant.
The government and the municipal corporation treated the institute as owner of the site.
issues.conclusion: The institute acquired title to the site by adverse possession, and the government’s challenge to its title failed.
issues.legal_principle: Possession under colour of an invalid grant, when it is not referable to a valid legal title, is prima facie adverse to the government’s title from its commencement. Open, as-of-right and uninterrupted possession for the required period can establish title by adverse possession. The court relied on Collector of Bombay v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay and applied that principle to the concurrent findings concerning possession and the treatment of the institute as owner.

rule.if: land_acquisition_title_appeal and possession_under_colour_of_invalid_grant and possession_open_continuous_uninterrupted and possession_exceeded_limitation_period and possessor_treated_as_owner

predicates.land_acquisition_title_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal disputing title to land relevant to a land-acquisition compensation claim.
predicates.possession_under_colour_of_invalid_grant: The possessor occupied the land under colour of a grant that was not legally valid.
predicates.possession_open_continuous_uninterrupted: The possessor’s occupation and enjoyment of the land were open, continuous and uninterrupted.
predicates.possession_exceeded_limitation_period: The possession continued for longer than the period required to acquire title by adverse possession.
predicates.possessor_treated_as_owner: The government or other relevant public authority treated the possessor as the owner of the land.

issues.definition: In an appeal disputing land title, possession under colour of an invalid grant that is open, uninterrupted, sufficiently long, and accompanied by treatment as owner results in title by adverse possession.
